items.summary: rpg-api consumes rulebooks/dnd5e, tools/spatial, tools/environments, tools/spawn
items.details: rpg-api imports: rulebooks/dnd5e (character, combat, initiative, monster, monstertraits, features, conditions, actions, combatabilities, spells, dungeon, gamectx, refs). tools/spatial (room layout, entity placement, GridType constants). tools/environments (dungeon graph persistence, connection graph). tools/spawn (entity placement adapter). rpg-api never imports mechanics/* or core/* directly — it always goes through rulebooks/dnd5e types. rpg-api stores character.Data (toolkit type) in Redis and reconstructs via LoadFromData.

items.summary: rpg-api hardcodes spatial.GridTypeHex and HexOrientationPointyTop in the encounter handler
items.details: Verified from rpg-api/docs/architecture/overview.md: encounter handler hardcodes spatial.GridTypeHex and spatial.HexOrientationPointyTop at six call sites (lines 157-158, 359-360, 569-570, 757-758, 822-823, 905-906). These spatial constants should come from the orchestrator's output, not be constructed in the handler. This is a violation on the rpg-api side, not the toolkit side — but toolkit needs to be aware that consumers may depend on the current hex-default behavior.

items.summary: rpg-api components/dungeon/ depends on dungeon generation logic that should be in toolkit
items.details: rpg-api/internal/components/dungeon/ implements procedural dungeon generation (room shapes, wall perimeters, door spawning, hex-grid layouts, monster CR budgets, theme tables). This violates the Boundary Rule — game mechanics belong in rpg-toolkit. The work item is to extract this to toolkit (tools/dungeon/ or a new module). Until then, rpg-api and toolkit have a silent duplication: dungeon logic in both repos.

items.summary: toolkit never imports rpg-api or rpg-api-protos — verified clean
items.details: Verified: grep -r 'rpg-api' */go.mod from toolkit root returns empty. No toolkit module imports rpg-api or rpg-api-protos. This is the correct direction. If any toolkit module ever needs a type that rpg-api has, the type must be defined locally in toolkit.

items.summary: game module version spread: v0.1.0 with events v0.1.1, while spatial uses events v0.6.2
items.details: game/go.mod pins events v0.1.1. tools/spatial/go.mod pins events v0.6.2. These are significantly different versions. game.Context is used in tools/spatial for LoadRoomFromContext. If events interface changed between v0.1.1 and v0.6.2 in ways that affect the EventBus type, there could be a compatibility gap. No runtime issue observed as of 2026-05-02, but watch for this when upgrading game.
